2 Chronicles 2:6.bridge: Solomon writes to Huram, king of Tyre, asking for cedar and skilled craftsmen, since the house he will build must be great, for God is great.

2 Chronicles 5:13.bridge: The temple is finished. Solomon assembles Israel, and the priests carry the ark into the most holy place while Levite singers and trumpeters stand by the altar.

2 Chronicles 6:12.bridge: Solomon blesses the people and recalls God's promise that David's son would build the temple.

2 Chronicles 10:16.bridge: The people ask Rehoboam to lighten Solomon's heavy yoke. Rejecting the elders' advice, he answers harshly: "My father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions."

2 Chronicles 13:4.bridge: Rehoboam dies and his son Abijah reigns over Judah. He goes to war against Jeroboam, whose army is twice the size of his.

2 Chronicles 13:15.bridge: Jeroboam's ambush surrounds Judah front and rear; they cry to the LORD and the priests sound the trumpets.

2 Chronicles 14:11.bridge: Abijah dies and his son Asa, a reformer who removes the idols, becomes king. When Zerah the Ethiopian invades with a huge army, Asa prays:

2 Chronicles 16:7.bridge: Years later, when Baasha king of Israel threatens Judah, Asa pays the king of Syria with temple treasure to attack Israel instead.

2 Chronicles 17:9.bridge: Jehoshaphat seeks the LORD and sends princes, Levites and priests through the cities of Judah.

2 Chronicles 18:13.bridge: Jehoshaphat allies with Ahab of Israel against Ramoth-gilead. Ahab's four hundred prophets promise victory, but Jehoshaphat asks for a prophet of the LORD, so Micaiah is summoned and urged to agree.

2 Chronicles 18:33.bridge: Micaiah sees God sending a lying spirit to Ahab's prophets. Ahab jails him and goes into battle in disguise.

2 Chronicles 19:6.bridge: Jehoshaphat returns home, is rebuked by a seer for helping Ahab, and appoints judges throughout Judah.

2 Chronicles 21:20.bridge: Jehoram leads Judah into idolatry. A letter from Elijah foretells his doom, and after raids by Philistines and Arabs he dies of a terrible disease.

2 Chronicles 22:10.bridge: Jehoram's youngest son Ahaziah reigns one year, guided by his mother Athaliah of Ahab's house, until Jehu kills him.

2 Chronicles 23:11.bridge: After six years hidden in the temple, the priest Jehoiada gathers the Levites and captains and arms them to guard the young prince.

2 Chronicles 24:20.bridge: Joash repairs the temple, but after Jehoiada dies he and the princes turn to idols and ignore the prophets.

2 Chronicles 25:1.bridge: A Syrian army defeats Judah, and Joash is murdered in his bed by his own servants.

2 Chronicles 28:9.bridge: Judah is defeated by Syria and by Israel, whose army carries off two hundred thousand captives toward Samaria.

2 Chronicles 28:15.bridge: Leaders of Ephraim support the prophet, and the soldiers release the captives and spoil.

2 Chronicles 29:27.bridge: The Levites cleanse the temple in sixteen days, and Hezekiah offers sin offerings for all Israel.

2 Chronicles 30:18.bridge: Though many scoff, some from the northern tribes come, and a great crowd gathers at Jerusalem for the feast.

2 Chronicles 32:7.bridge: Hezekiah blocks the springs outside the city, rebuilds the walls, and rallies his captains:

2 Chronicles 32:21.bridge: Sennacherib's envoys mock the LORD before the people on the wall, and Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah cry to heaven.

2 Chronicles 33:1.bridge: Hezekiah dies, and his son Manasseh succeeds him.

2 Chronicles 34:1.bridge: Manasseh's son Amon reigns wickedly for two years until his servants kill him; his son Josiah is made king.

2 Chronicles 34:27.bridge: Josiah sends to the prophetess Huldah, who declares that the book's curses will fall on Judah, but has this message for the king:

2 Chronicles 35:24.bridge: Josiah ignores Necho's warning, fights him at Megiddo, and is badly wounded by archers.

2 Chronicles 36:12.bridge: Josiah's sons and grandson reign briefly under Egypt and then Babylon, whose king Nebuchadnezzar deports them in turn and makes Zedekiah the last king of Judah.
